eligibility.evidence: Sections 1-3: a 124M-parameter GPT-2 Dutch-English model pre-trained by the authors is the subject (small, self-trained, so E1 'any size' is borderline); crosslingual structural priming (Bock 1986; Schoonbaert et al. 2007) is a cited psycholinguistic paradigm; new target-sentence probabilities analysed with a mixed-effects model.

A.title: Crosslingual Structural Priming and the Pre-Training Dynamics of Bilingual Language Models

models.name: Dutch-English bilingual GPT-2 (124M), pre-trained from scratch by the authors
models.version: 1M pre-training steps, batch 128; checkpoints analysed across training

paradigms.name: Crosslingual (Dutch prime to English target) structural priming, dative alternation (PO vs DO)
paradigms.source_paper: Schoonbaert et al. 2007; Bock 1986; Loebell & Bock 2003

effects.label: NO-HUMAN-REFERENCE
effects.location: Section 3 (prime type x step interaction chi2(20)=56.86, p<0.001; first significant at step 500120, t(3943)=2.93, adj. p=0.030); Fig. 1, p.2

E.headline: Crosslingual structural priming emerges within about 1M English tokens after exposure to the second language, implying shared abstract structure and possible contamination-driven zero-shot transfer.

G.notes: Tiny self-trained model, not a deployed LLM; no human data, so no comparison to human priming magnitude. Stimulus list and item count not given; no code link. Effects before step 500K attributed to English contamination without test.
